passages.quote: The Ome road was run north to south through the middle, and on both sides of it, after the sixty-six provinces of Japan, the house lots were divided into strips, one household's with a frontage of nine ken, thirty-three lots each, and settlers were recruited to live there. That the front yards were made wide though the lots' frontage was narrow is said to be because there was a plan to hold a market in future and make a post town.
passages.original: 南北中央に青梅街道を通し、その両側に日本の六六州にちなんで屋敷割を一軒分、間口九間として三三区画ずつの短冊形に分け、出百姓を募って住まわせた。屋敷の間口が狭い割に前庭を広くとったのは、将来市を立て宿場町をつくる計画があったからだといわれている。

passages.quote: the headman of Shimo-Morooka village, Yoshino Oribenosuke, in the Keicho era (1596-1615), cleared the wilderness stretching from Ome to Hakonegasaki.
passages.original: 下師岡村の名主吉野織部之助が慶長年間（1596～1615)に、青梅から箱根ヶ崎にわたる原野を切り開いた。

passages.quote: As befits a new-field development, the main houses stand along the highway and the fields spread out behind in strips
passages.original: 新田開発らしく、街道沿いに主屋があって、短冊状に畑が広がる

footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: The natural levee is a slight rise against the backswamp spreading on the channel side and behind it (the side away from the channel), and drains well within low, wet alluvial lowland. For that reason, on alluvial lowland, long-established settlements are sited first of all on the natural levees, which are also used as dry fields.
passages.original: 自然堤防は流路側および背後（流路と反対側）に広がる後背湿地に対してわずかな高まりとなり、低湿な沖積低地の中では水はけが良い。そのために沖積低地において、古くからの集落はまず自然堤防上に立地し、また畑として利用される

footnotes.assertion: On low ground the line was the land's own: a dike on land reclaimed from the sea, or the slight rise of a river's natural levee, which drained well above the wet ground behind it.

passages.quote: a dry-field new field of the Genroku period (1688-1704), lying in the northeast of the Musashino plateau.

passages.quote: Roads 6 ken wide (about 11 m) were opened lengthwise and crosswise, and along them, with a frontage of 40 ken (about 73 m) and a depth of 375 ken as one lot, the houses and the farmland were set out in strips.

passages.quote: In 1694 the domain lord Yanagisawa Yasuaki ordered his retainer Sone Gondayu and others to settle farmers from nearby villages there, and in 1696 a land survey was made and the villages founded.
passages.original: 1694年藩主柳沢保明が家臣曾根権太夫らに命じて近村の農民を入植させ，1696年検地を行って立村。

passages.quote: In the south of the plateau the linear villages are formed in the direction of the canals dug along the highways, and in the north, because the water source is wells, in a comparatively free direction.
passages.original: 台地南部は街道にそって掘られた用水路の方向に、北部は水源が井戸のため比較的自由な方向に、列村が形成されている。

footnotes.assertion: On the Musashino plateau the rows followed canals in the south and ran freely in the north.In the south of the plateau the rows run with the canals dug along the highways; in the north, where the water came from wells, they run in a comparatively free direction.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: A long-established settlement developing in a curve beside the river and its old channel (upper right), and new housing on the backswamp (outskirts of Niigata)
passages.original: 河川や旧河道（右上）脇に曲線状に発達する古くからの集落と後背湿地の新興住宅地（新潟市郊外）

footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: Settlements are often sited at the fan head, where the valley stream's water can be had before it sinks into the fan, or at the fan's foot, where the water that has flowed underground through the fan is had as springs.
passages.original: 集落は谷川の水が扇状地に浸透する以前の水の得られる扇頂か、扇状地を伏流してきた水が湧水となって得られる扇端に立地する例が多い。

passages.quote: In the western foothills of the Shuso plain fine alluvial fans stand in a row.
passages.original: 周桑平野の西部山麓には見事な扇状地が並んでいる。

passages.quote: At the foot of the Sekiya river's fan many settlements are lined up in a row, drawing an arc
passages.original: 関屋川の扇状地の扇端には、多くの集落が孤を描いて列状に並んでいるが

footnotes.assertion: On the Shuso plain of Iyo, settlements often sit at an alluvial fan's head or, where the water that sank into the fan rises again as springs, at its foot, and at the foot of the Sekiya river's fan many of them line up in an arc.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

footnotes.assertion: No page we read says which line was commoner, a road laid first or the land's own.The pages name rows along a road and along a dike, a levee and a fan's foot, and none counts one kind against another.

passages.quote: Traditional village boundaries in the mountainous area of southwest Zhejiang are mainly clusters and bands, which are restricted by geographical conditions and tend to expand in the direction of rivers and roads.

footnotes.assertion: In mountainous southwest Zhejiang, villages tended to grow along rivers and roads.The traditional villages there form mainly clusters and bands, and tend to grow along rivers and roads.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: A road village, on the other hand, is one where the dwellings stand in line along a comparatively narrow street, on one side of it or on both, depending little on the street, and formed chiefly as a farming settlement.
passages.original: これに対して路村というのは、比較的狭い街路に沿って民家が、その片側または両側に並列し、街路への依存度が少なく、主として農業集落として形成されているものに該当する。

footnotes.assertion: A row's farms stood on one side of its line or on both.A road village is defined as a farming settlement whose houses stand along a fairly narrow street, on one side of it or on both;
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: A settlement whose houses stand in line on one side or both sides of a street, taking a long, thin shape; also called a linear village.
passages.original: 街路の片側または両側に家が建ち並び細長い形状を呈する集落で、列状村落ともいう。

footnotes.assertion: A row's farms stood on one side of its line or on both.A road village is defined as a farming settlement whose houses stand along a fairly narrow street, on one side of it or on both; the linear village too has its houses on one side or both.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: The four Nobidome Shinden villages founded in Kanbun 1 (1661) (Nobidome, Sugasawa, Nishibori and Kitano) are known to have had a strip-shaped field form some 400 ken deep, in which house lot, farmland and moor followed one another on both sides of the Kawagoe road.
passages.original: 寛文元年（1661）に成立した野火止新田4か村（野火止村、菅沢村、西堀村、北野村）は、川越街道の両側に屋敷地・耕地・野が続くという奥行き400間程度の短冊形の耕地形態であったことが知られています。

passages.quote: a road 6 ken (10.8 m) wide was run through, and on both sides of it house lot, farmland and coppice were each set out in strips.
passages.original: 幅6間（10.8m）の道路を通し、両側にそれぞれ屋敷・耕地・雑木林を短冊形に配置しました。

footnotes.assertion: Santome's lots lay on both sides of its road, and so did Nobidome's.Santome's house lots, fields and coppice were set out in strips on both sides of its road, and the lots of the Nobidome villages of 1661 lay the same way along the Kawagoe road.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: (1) As a rule the homestead is covered by its homestead grove, but today the groves have much decreased. (2) As to the use of the homestead, the main house faces south, and round its front yard the workshop, garage, barn, privy and the like are placed; some houses have a well or a homestead god. On the road side zelkova and white oak are planted, and these form an avenue. And the paths called "ainomichi" and "niwadoshi" are laid, linking homestead to homestead sideways.
passages.original: ①屋敷は屋敷林に覆われているのが基本であるが，現在では，屋敷林がかなり減少している。②屋敷内の使われ方は，母屋が南面し，この前庭を中心に作業所，車庫，納屋，便所などが配置され，井戸や屋敷神などのある家がある。道路側はケヤキ・シラカシが植えられ，これが並木を形成している。また屋敷と屋敷を横につなぐ「アイノミチ」「ニワドウシ」が設けられている。

passages.quote: The street villages common on the Kanto plain have the new-field farmers' houses in line on both sides of the highway, each with its owned farmland behind it made in a strip-shaped division of equal area, and are called planned pioneer road villages.
passages.original: 関東平野に多い街村は街道の両側に新田百姓の家屋が並び，それぞれの背後に所有耕地が均等な面積をもって短冊状の土地割りをなして作られ，計画的開拓路村といわれる。

footnotes.assertion: On a planned row, each farm's field lay behind its house, and its woodland beyond.Santome's land ran back from the road as house lot, then field, then woodland; the planned road villages of the Kanto plain set each house's holding behind it in strips of equal area.

passages.quote: This form, the same as what is called the forest village of northern Germany, well shows the character of a pioneer settlement.
passages.original: この形態は、北ドイツの林地村落とよばれるものと同じく、開拓集落の特徴をよく表す。

passages.quote: the field each household itself worked was placed near its homestead, and at its far end the plain woodland was placed, as the source of fodder for livestock and of green manure, compost and other means of keeping up the soil, together with fuel and other materials of daily life.
passages.original: 各戸の屋敷の近くに自ら耕作する畑地を配し、その先端に平地林を配置して、家畜の飼料、草肥・堆肥など地力維持資材とともに燃料など生活資材の供給源としたのであった。

footnotes.assertion: The woodland at the strip's far end gave fodder, compost and fuel - the same form, the page notes, as the north German forest village.
footnotes.question: 0033-row-villages-resson.html

passages.quote: On reclaimed new fields the farmhouses line up on the dike of land reclaimed from the sea and form a linear village, and land reclaimed from a lake has many linear villages running round the old lakeshore. The farmed land is near the house and comparatively compact.

footnotes.assertion: On reclaimed ground, a farm's land lay near the house and fairly compact.Where the row stood on a dike, the farmed land was near the house and comparatively compact, no strip named.

North of the main house it is mainly zelkova with a little white oak mixed in, but as a homestead grove it has become rather thin.
passages.original: この地に寛文年間（１６６１～１６７１）に移り住んだ小川町のＢ家の場合は、青梅街道から枝分かれした立川街道が屋敷の北側を走る。母屋の北側はケヤキを主として、シラカシが少しまじるが、屋敷林としては割合うすくなっている。

passages.quote: What is unusual is that a grove of madake bamboo grows widely all along the south side of the homestead. North of the main house, across the Tachikawa and Ome roads, houses with homestead groves stand in a row to the north, so no bamboo is especially needed there for a windbreak, and it was made on the south side, they say, and basket makers used to come often to buy the bamboo

passages.quote: At this house, they say, the bamboo grove was on the south side; this is connected with the homestead lying on the south side of the road, and with the houses with homestead groves forming a row settlement across the road to the north.
